vectors.enisa_quote: communications are affected by the amount of traffic sent
vectors.reason: ENISA says traffic is sent but not by whom; traffic and commands reach the satellite from outside the mission over the TT&C radio link.

vectors.enisa_quote: components such as the payload receive commands to sense, emit, or run whatever mission the satellite has
vectors.reason: The text states the effect (the payload keeps receiving mission commands), not who sends them; commands the satellite honours under SDLS come from the mission's own ground system or an insider, which is an inference from the text.

vectors.enisa_quote: communications are affected by the amount of traffic sent
vectors.reason: The assets include payload communications (PLCOM); user traffic on the service link is the traffic a terminal sends, but ENISA does not name terminals.

rows.sparta_quote: any actor-controlled transmitter, platform, or node
rows.reason: An outside transmitter or terminal is how traffic beyond the mission's own volume reaches the satellite.

rows.sparta_quote: Adversaries may field their own ground system, transportable or fixed, to transmit and receive mission-compatible signals
rows.reason: A rogue ground station sends the mission commands the payload keeps honouring.

rows.sparta_quote: transmit legitimate-looking commands to the target spacecraft
rows.reason: Commands the satellite honours repeatedly, 'whatever mission', come from a valid ground system.

rows.enisa_quote: communications are affected by the amount of traffic sent
rows.sparta_quote: Flooding overwhelms a communication or processing path by injecting traffic
rows.reason: Excess traffic is how ENISA says communications are exhausted.

rows.enisa_quote: receive commands to sense, emit, or run whatever mission the satellite has
rows.sparta_quote: saturates paths with legitimate telecommands or bus messages so the spacecraft burns scarce resources honoring them
rows.reason: Commands sent constantly so the satellite burns scarce resources honouring them is the satellite-operations exhaustion ENISA describes.

rows.enisa_quote: run whatever mission the satellite has - contstantly
rows.sparta_quote: The adversary may misuse a function by activating it at the wrong time, repeating it, interrupting it, or directing it toward an unintended purpose.
rows.reason: Driving the payload's sense, emit or mission functions without pause is a repeated use of a native function; it is what drains the battery.

rows.enisa_quote: to the point that the battery is fully drained/depleted
rows.sparta_quote: The resource may support computing, storage, or communications.
rows.reason: Battery, storage and communications depletion are the stated outcomes; SPARTA's text also covers power as a resource.
